G1.statement: No Saudi health-sector AI governance policy for non-device AI

G2.statement: No general human-in-the-loop or override obligation outside the medical-device route

G3.statement: No Saudi statute on electronic health records as such

G4.statement: Anonymisation and re-identification risk assessment are mandated with no published method

G5.statement: No Saudi regime validates or benchmarks health-AI model performance

G6.statement: No governance of AI output disclosure or communication

G7.statement: Governing telehealth instrument lapsed 31 Dec 2021 with no successor

G9.statement: Nothing addresses Arabic dialect variation or accessibility in health AI

G10.statement: AI is entirely absent from the national cybersecurity baseline

G11.statement: No national standard defines what a complete referral document must contain

field_definitions.binding: Creates a legal obligation on a healthcare provider operating in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
field_definitions.scope_limit: A limit in the instrument's own stated scope that excludes a non-device clinical AI system deployed in a Saudi hospital. Where present, the instrument cannot govern a concern for this system.
field_definitions.scope_note: A narrower applicability caveat recorded for transparency; does not by itself remove the instrument from scope.
field_definitions.governs: Concerns from node_concerns that this instrument actually governs. Curated legal judgement, open to challenge.
field_definitions.governs_without_method: Concerns where this instrument imposes a duty but publishes no method by which compliance can be demonstrated or audited. Produces a METHOD GAP.
